27 An outdoor concert has two large speakers beside the stage for broadcasting music.
In order to test the speakers, they are made to emit sound of the same wavelength and the same
amplitude.
The curved lines in the diagram represent wavefronts.
Where is the loudest sound heard?
A
C
D
B
speakers
stage

hints: Notice the curved lines are crests of sound waves from the two speakers, which have the same wavelength and act as coherent sources.
Recall that loudest sound means maximum amplitude from constructive interference, which needs crest to meet crest with path difference $n\lambda$.
Compare points A, B, C and D with the crossings of the two sets of arcs to find which point sits on two overlapping wavefronts.
walkthrough: The two speakers emit sound of the same wavelength and amplitude, so they act as coherent sources that produce a two-source interference pattern.
Loudness follows amplitude. Loudest sound is heard where the two waves interfere constructively to give maximum resultant amplitude.
For sound waves, constructive interference occurs when crest meets crest, which needs path difference $= n\lambda$ where $n = 0, 1, 2...$.
On a wavefront diagram, crests are drawn as lines, so crest-meets-crest positions are where a line from the left speaker intersects a line from the right speaker.
Points A, B and C do not sit on such a double crossing. Each sits on or near a crest from one speaker but between crests from the other speaker, so the superposition gives reduced amplitude.
Point D sits exactly on the intersection of a left-speaker wavefront and a right-speaker wavefront, so the two displacements add in phase.
This constructive point has the largest vibration amplitude and therefore the loudest sound. This is option D.

A.explanation: Point A lies on a wavefront from one speaker but about half a wavelength from a wavefront from the other speaker, so the interference is not fully constructive and the sound is not maximum.

B.explanation: Point B does not lie on the crossing of two wavefronts, so a crest from one speaker does not meet a crest from the other speaker and the resultant amplitude is small.

C.explanation: Point C lies between wavefronts and not on a double wavefront crossing, so the path difference is not $n\lambda$ and constructive interference does not occur there.

D.explanation: Point D lies exactly where a wavefront from the left speaker crosses a wavefront from the right speaker, so crest meets crest to give constructive interference and maximum loudness.
